newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FOCUS - Lisbon bourse euphoria can't last - analysts.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS - Lisbon bourse euphoria can't last - analysts.

text.p: The Lisbon bourse, which has shown double digit-growth in the first two weeks of 1997, is in euphoric mood but analysts warned on Wednesday that the market could ease back soon as investors took profits.
The PSI-20 .PSI20 index of 20 leading stocks, currently around 5,700 and just below record levels, has gained about 11 percent since January 2.
"I'm starting to get a little concerned," said Juan Simon, chief equities analyst at Banco Efisa. "I'm starting to think the market might take a little rest."

A sustained drop in official interest rates in recent months, including the latest 20 basis point cut in the repo rate last Friday, has lifted stock prices as companies pay less to service debt, boosting their earnings per share.

Bond yields have plunged as the Socialist government has made progress to meet tough entry targets for joining a European single currency, causing investment houses to divert funds to Lisbon stocks which give better returns.
Analysts expect the Bank of Portugal to cut interest rates further this year.

Domestic and international investment houses and pension funds are buying aggressively on the Lisbon bourse, local dealers and analysts said. Turnover on the bourse surged following several state sell-offs.

Some said they believed that Morgan Stanley Capital International's (MSCI) Geneva-based Capital International subsidiary would soon move the Portuguese equity market from its emerging market indices to its European indices.
A spokesman for MSCI declined comment, saying: "There is strictly nothing we can say in response to this."

A move from the emerging market indices to the European indices could presage a flow of funds into the Portuguese market as fund managers use the MSCI benchmarks to allocate assets and measure performance.
Portugal Telecom and mobile phone operator Telecel have pulled Lisbon bourse higher this year.
Increased demand for mobile phones in Portugal and expectations of healthy results have stimulated buying interest.

Bank stocks have shown an unimpressive performance as their results are not expected to show a dramatic improvement, analysts said. Some banks are restructuring after mergers and absorbing goodwill from acquisitions.

Increased interest in Portuguese stocks fuelled by the success of recent privatisations and falling interest rates augurs well for the sell-off of state assets later this year, notably energy company EDP-Electricidade de Portugal.
But the market was not poised for an uninterrupted bull run, analysts said.
One analyst at a Lisbon broker, who asked not to be identified, said: "I don't know how much the correction will be but the rise cannot last much more."
Dealers said the market was poised to take profits as investors believed the underlying performance of some companies did not justify the surge in their share prices to date.
"The buying does not result from brokers' recommendations," said one foreign analyst. "The fundamentals of some companies, especially smaller ones, do not justify this level of buying."
Lisbon bourse is vulnerable to sell-offs in foreign markets, especially Wall Street, analysts added.
